constraints: Dependency age: new Cargo.lock entries must be >=7 days old (AGENTS.md); tree-sitter-php 0.25.2 GitHub tag is 2026-11-19, so it clears this by about one day; SKIP_PACKAGE_AGE_CHECK must not be used (issue).

Workspace tree-sitter is 0.27.1 (Cargo.toml) and 0.27.2 is locked; tree-sitter-php 0.25.2 targets tree-sitter 0.27 for dev-dependencies and depends on tree-sitter-language 0.1 at runtime, so the ABI is shared, not duplicated.
LanguageInfo.element_query and call_query are non-Option &'static str; CALL_QUERY must be a string (css.rs uses "" when there are no calls).

LanguageInfo.defuse_query is Option<&str>, so the compiler does not require DEFUSE_QUERY; the requirement comes from the issue's acceptance criteria and from parser.rs:562 (defuse None returns empty results).
get_ts_language must return LANGUAGE_PHP (mixed HTML + PHP) for the HTML-template criterion; LANGUAGE_PHP_ONLY is a second entry point exported by the crate.
Query compilation is lazy (QUERY_CACHE, OnceLock per language); a broken query is found at first analysis, so a unit test must compile every query (issue step 3).

Symbol matching in defuse compares node text to the symbol name; capturing (name) inside variable_name matches 'x' without the $ sigil, while a bare (name) capture would also match function, class and method names, so read captures must be restricted to variable_name.
Maintainers implement this in-house; the issue says external pull requests will be closed, so Scout output should go to maintainers.

Scope limits from the issue: no extract_function_name, find_method_for_receiver or find_receiver_type; no trait use resolution, property or constant extraction, attributes or namespace aliasing; no .phtml, .inc, .module or .php5 extensions; no tool handler or schema change.
Workspace lints deny unwrap_used, expect_used and undocumented_unsafe_blocks; tests are exempt via cfg_attr in each crate's lib.rs.
Binary size delta must be stated in the PR description (issue, and #1063); it cannot be measured without a build, which this read-only scout did not run.

approaches.name: A. Full OO-precedent integration with mixed-HTML grammar (recommended)
approaches.description: Recommended. Mirror the Java and Swift OO-language shape: new crates/aptu-coder-core/src/languages/php.rs with ELEMENT_QUERY (func_name/method_name/class_name captures, outer @function/@class), CALL_QUERY (function_call_expression function: (name), member_call_expression name: (name), scoped_call_expression name: (name), all captured as @call), REFERENCE_QUERY ((named_type (name) @type_ref)), IMPORT_QUERY ((namespace_use_declaration) @import_path), DEFUSE_QUERY (as drafted), and extract_inheritance (kind-walk as described in inheritance_walk_citation, not field lookups). Skip extract_function_name, find_method_for_receiver and find_receiver_type (issue scope). Register tree_sitter_php::LANGUAGE_PHP (the mixed HTML+PHP entry point; LANGUAGE_PHP_ONLY would not handle the HTML-template acceptance criterion) in get_language_info and get_ts_language. Wire Cargo.toml workspace dep tree-sitter-php = "0.25.2", core Cargo.toml dep, EXTENSION_MAP ('php','php'), supported_languages(), mod.rs pub mod php and the test table row, lang.rs test assertion, README intro count and list, and one integration test file in crates/aptu-coder/tests/.
pros: Satisfies every acceptance criterion in the issue, including the five query constants and the HTML-template case.
Same shape as java.rs and swift.rs, so reviewers and parser_elements.rs capture contracts already fit.
DEFUSE_QUERY enables def-use results for PHP; without it extract_def_use_for_file returns empty for php.
Grammar node kinds and fields were checked against node-types.json at tag v0.25.2, reducing query-compile risk.
cons: Largest surface: about 8 files including Cargo.lock, README and a new integration test file.
Several draft queries (defuse, reference) are not compiled yet; a unit test must prove compilation before wiring, per the issue's suggested approach.
Inheritance must walk unfielded children by kind, which is more code than Java's field lookup.
A defuse symbol match compares node text, so PHP symbols are matched without the $ sigil (the name node, not variable_name).

approaches.name: B. Minimal registry integration (element, call, import, inheritance only)
approaches.description: Same php.rs skeleton, but reference_query and defuse_query are set to None in the LanguageInfo arm, and only ELEMENT_QUERY, CALL_QUERY, IMPORT_QUERY and extract_inheritance carry content. Wiring is identical to A. The LanguageInfo defuse_query field is Option<&str>, so the struct compiles either way.
pros: Smallest query-risk surface; fewer patterns to validate.
Fastest path to a working analyze_file for functions, classes and inheritance.
cons: Violates the issue's acceptance criterion that php.rs has all five query constants.
extract_def_use_for_file returns vec![] when compiled.defuse is None (parser.rs:562), so def-use for PHP silently returns nothing.

Diverges from every OO precedent in mod.rs, where defuse_query is Some for java, kotlin, swift, csharp, cpp, go, rust, python, typescript and javascript; only fortran, markdown, css and yaml use None.

approaches.name: C. Tags-driven queries derived from upstream queries/tags.scm
approaches.description: Start ELEMENT_QUERY and REFERENCE_QUERY from upstream queries/tags.scm (definition.function, definition.method, definition.class, definition.interface, definition.trait, reference.implementation, reference.call) and rename captures to the parser_elements.rs contract (function, func_name, method_name, class, class_name). Hand-write the enum pattern, since the tags.scm content read in this scout (the full file through reference.call) has no enum_declaration pattern. Hand-write DEFUSE_QUERY. Same wiring as A.
pros: Reuses patterns maintained by the grammar authors for declarations and call sites.
reference.implementation pattern (class_interface_clause [(name) (qualified_name)]) gives a ready implements capture.
cons: tags.scm capture names (definition.*, reference.*) do not match parser_elements.rs; every capture must be renamed anyway.
No enum pattern in tags.scm, so enums still need a hand-written pattern.
Upstream tags.scm targets editor tagging, not analysis outputs, so it may return more matches than the element contract expects (for example, nested class-like nodes).

recommendation: Approach A. It is the only option that meets every acceptance criterion in #1864 (five query constants, implements/extends contract, HTML-template parse, def-use coverage) and it copies the Java/Swift shape that the parser already expects. Use tree_sitter_php::LANGUAGE_PHP, not LANGUAGE_PHP_ONLY, because the HTML-template criterion depends on the mixed grammar: the grammar's extras include text_interpolation, so HTML between ?> and <?php parses with no ERROR nodes (verify with the unit test). Pin tree-sitter-php = "0.25.2" (GitHub tag published 2026-11-19T16:26:36Z; the cargo-deny package age check needs >=7 days, so it passes at about 8 days old; crates.io publish time was not checkable here, so confirm before pinning, and fall back to 0.25.1 published 2026-10-06 if needed). tree-sitter-php depends on tree-sitter-language = "0.1", which is already locked at 0.1.9, so no new tree-sitter-language entry is expected. Caveat: the issue states maintainers are implementing this in-house and external PRs will be closed, so this scout output is for the maintainers, not an external PR.

inheritance_walk_citation: Grammar source inspected: tree-sitter-php tag v0.25.2, php/src/grammar.json (rules), php/src/node-types.json (fields/children), and php/grammar.js which calls common/define-grammar.js (Context7 quotes the same rules). (1) Entry node: a class_declaration. Its rule is optional FIELD attributes, REPEAT _modifier, keyword 'class' (ALIAS PATTERN 'class'), FIELD name (RESERVED 'classes' name), CHOICE[base_clause | BLANK], CHOICE[class_interface_clause | BLANK], FIELD body declaration_list. node-types.json lists only three fields on class_declaration: attributes, body, name. No field named superclass, interfaces, base_classes or parent_class exists, so child_by_field_name cannot reach the clauses (unlike java.rs, which uses superclass/interfaces). (2) Extends: iterate named_child(i) of the class_declaration and select kind == 'base_clause' (an unfielded child). base_clause rule = ALIAS 'extends' followed by SEQ(_name, REPEAT(',' _name)). node-types.json children of base_clause: name, qualified_name, relative_name. For each named child of base_clause whose kind is name, qualified_name or relative_name, emit format!("extends {}", source[start_byte..end_byte]). (3) Implements: iterate named_child(i) of the class_declaration and select kind == 'class_interface_clause' (unfielded). Rule = ALIAS 'implements' followed by SEQ(_name, REPEAT(',' _name)); children name, qualified_name, relative_name. Emit format!("implements {}", text) for each. (4) Ordering: named children are visited in source order, so extends entries precede implements entries. The class name (field name) is never emitted. (5) No clauses: neither child exists, so the result is an empty Vec, which matches the issue edge case. (6) Interfaces: interface_declaration has only base_clause (node-types.json children: base_clause), which holds the multi-parent 'extends A, B' list; a handler that also accepts interface_declaration would emit extends entries from the same base_clause walk. trait_declaration and enum_declaration have no base_clause or class_interface_clause child in the grammar (enum_declaration children include class_interface_clause and primitive_type, so enums do have an implements clause). Expected output for 'class Foo extends Bar implements A, B {}': ["extends Bar", "implements A", "implements B"]. Confirmed upstream parse shape (Context7, corpus declarations.txt): (class_declaration name: (name) (base_clause (name)) body: (declaration_list ...)) and (class_interface_clause (name)).
